newsitem.title: USA: CME letter calls hand-held computers a priority.
newsitem.headline: CME letter calls hand-held computers a priority.

text.p: Implementing the use of hand-held computers to record local traders' transactions is a "major priority" for the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME), according to a letter from CME Chairman Jack Sandner.
In a letter to members distributed on the trading floor Tuesday, Sandner noted plans for more hand-held computers at the CME.
U.S. regulators have asked U.S. exchanges to come up with more accurate trade-tracking devices.

"We have deployed three hand-helds with a plan to support up to 50 in 1997," Sandner wrote. "Other exchanges, primarily the CBOE (Chicago Board Options Exchange), have successfully deployed this technology, which is a good benchmark to demonstrate that it can be effective," he wrote.
